newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore TPC starts up polyethylene plant.
newsitem.headline: Singapore TPC starts up polyethylene plant.

text.p: The Polyethylene Co (TPC), a subsidiary of Sumitomo Chemicals, has started producing on-specification polyethyelene last weekend, a Sumitomo official said on Tuesday.
TPC will also produce on-specification polypropylene in the next few days at the new U.S.$400 million plant, Akio Kosai, president of Sumitomo Chemicals told Reuters.
The new plant will produce 70,000 tonnes of low density polyethylene (LDPE), 120,000 tonnes of linear low density polyethylene (LLDPE) and 120,000 tonnes of polypropylene (PP) annually.
TPC already produces 160,000 tonnes of LDPE and 193,000 tonnes of PP annually.
The plant, which is 51-percent owned by Sumitomo Chemicals, is part of the Singapore $3.4 billion (U.S$2.36 billion) expansion project of the Singapore Petrochemical Complex.
The complex is located on Pulau Ayer Merbau and Pulau Seraya, two islands off southwestern Singapore.
The expansion is centred around a new 515,000-tonne-per-year ethylene plant operated by the Petrochemical Corporation of Singapore (PCS).
PCS, which already operates a 450,000-tonne-per-year ethylene plant, started up the new cracker over the weekend.
PCS is 50-percent owned by a Sumitomo Chemicals led consortium of Japanese companies with Royal Dutch Shell taking the remaining 50 percent.
